title: lnd custom macaroons inherit the target user's login group, leaking to shared 'users' group
description: The root ExecStartPost creates /run/lnd/<name>.macaroon as root:root 0440, then runs `chown <user>:` (empty group). Per chown(1), a trailing colon with no group sets the group to the user's LOGIN group. For a macaroon granted to a normal login user (NixOS default primary group 'users', gid 100), the macaroon becomes readable by every normal user on the system, widening the grant beyond the named user. Shipped config is unaffected (the only defined macaroon targets system user 'btcpayserver', whose login group is its own), so this is config-dependent: it bites only when an operator defines services.lnd.macaroons.<n>.user as a regular login account. /run/lnd is mode 711, so group members can traverse to the file.
impact: A macaroon intended for one login user is readable by all users in group 'users'; depending on the macaroon's permissions (e.g. invoices:write, onchain:read) this is an unintended privilege/隐私 grant.
recommendation: Resolve the group explicitly instead of relying on login-group semantics: e.g. a dedicated per-macaroon group, or `chown <user>:nogroup` plus an ACL, or document that macaroon `user` must be a system user with a same-named group.

title: update-nix-bitcoin auto-selects the newest unsigned release tag; integrity rests on advisory operator review
description: update-nix-bitcoin picks the highest CalVer tag via `git ls-remote --tags ... | sort -V | tail -n1`, resolves it to a commit with two further ls-remote calls (re-targetable between calls), prefetches that commit's tarball, and writes the pin. There is no signature check on the tag or commit, although commits are SSH-signed (SECURITY.md documents tags as unsigned CI pointers). The written pin is self-consistent (commit + prefetched narHash) and the helper correctly refuses to auto-exec the new shell, printing a compare URL. But nothing forces the review: an operator who skips it and re-enters nix-shell evaluates the newly pinned tree's shellHook. This is weaker than the refused upstream helper (helper/fetch-release), which GPG-verifies the nar-hash against a pinned key. Repo/tag compromise (or a maliciously pushed '20*' tag by anyone with tag-push rights) flows into the pin with only a human gate.
impact: Supply-chain: a re-pointed or attacker-created tag yields an operator-approved-looking pin of unreviewed code. Mitigated by commit pinning, the printed compare URL, and no automatic shell re-entry.
recommendation: Verify the resolved commit's SSH signature against the maintainer's allowed-signers entry before writing the pin (the infrastructure exists: commits are signed), or at minimum fail unless the tag is an annotated tag object created by the CI workflow identity.

title: netns-exec leaks the netns fd into the executed program (missing O_CLOEXEC)
description: `open(netns_path, O_RDONLY)` lacks O_CLOEXEC, so the fd survives execv into the operator-chosen program running inside the namespace. The exec'd process runs as the unprivileged operator with all capabilities dropped, and setns() on the leaked fd requires CAP_SYS_ADMIN, so no privilege gain was found; if the exec target is itself setuid/file-capable, that target already has the powers the fd would grant. Pure hygiene.
impact: None demonstrated; leaked fd is unusable without CAP_SYS_ADMIN.

title: wireguard preset binds lnd admin REST to 0.0.0.0; protection is firewall-only
description: With lndconnect enabled the preset sets services.lnd.restAddress = 0.0.0.0 and relies on nixos-fw (default-drop + `-i wg-nb -s <peer>/32 --dport 8080` accept + restrictPeer REJECT inserted at top of nixos-fw/FORWARD) as the sole barrier. Since the last commit, evaluation refuses a disabled firewall and the nftables backend, closing the two silent-failure paths, and the accept rule is interface- and single-peer-scoped. Residual: any future local netfilter misconfiguration (or a local process binding/forwarding) exposes the macaroon-admin API; there is no defense in depth at the bind layer. The rebind to the WG server address is deliberately deferred with a breakage checklist in docs/wireguard-rest-bind.md, and lnd's restlisten=0.0.0.0 is IPv4-only so there is no parallel IPv6 gap.
impact: Single-point-of-failure on iptables for an admin-grade API; currently guarded and CI-gated (wireguard-lndconnect scenario).
recommendation: Work through docs/wireguard-rest-bind.md and bind to the WG server address; until then, consider also asserting services.lnd.restAddress == 0.0.0.0 only when the accept rule is in place.

title: bitcoind RPC cookie is group-readable (0640, group bitcoin) = full privileged RPC for group members
description: postStart chmods the RPC cookie 0640 root... owned bitcoin:bitcoin. Every member of group bitcoin (the operator, plus any service an operator adds to the group) holds full privileged RPC including wallet operations when the wallet is enabled (disablewallet defaults to unset). This is the upstream convenience design, annotated in-tree as audit L-10 with guidance to use rpc users + HMAC for new services. Reported for completeness because 'privilege boundaries we claim to provide' are in scope per SECURITY.md.
impact: Any process running as a group-bitcoin user can spend from the bitcoind wallet via RPC.
recommendation: Long-term, move local consumers to dedicated rpc users with HMAC and make the cookie root-only; at minimum keep group-bitcoin membership under review.

title: wireguard preset: restrictPeer silently inert when firewall is disabled and lndconnect is off
description: The preset asserts against nftables unconditionally but only asserts firewall.enable on the lndconnect (0.0.0.0 REST) path. With services.lnd.lndconnect.enable = false, nix-bitcoin.wireguard.restrictPeer = true (default) and networking.firewall.enable = false, evaluation succeeds while the restrictPeer iptables rules are never installed (extraCommands only run when the firewall is enabled), so the documented restriction contract silently does not hold.
impact: The WireGuard peer can reach any port on any node address. Practical impact is low because a disabled firewall already exposes the whole node by explicit user choice, but the preset's stated guarantee is false in this configuration and the assertion gating is internally inconsistent.
preconditions: Import wireguard preset; lndconnect disabled (or lnd disabled); networking.firewall.enable = false.
recommendation: Add assertion: !cfg.restrictPeer || config.networking.firewall.enable (or set restrictPeer default to false when the firewall is off), keeping it symmetric with the existing nftables assertion.

title: lnd admin REST API bound to 0.0.0.0 by the wireguard preset (known, deferred)
description: Enabling lndconnect with the wireguard preset moves the macaroon-authenticated admin REST API from localhost to all interfaces. Protection relies entirely on the nixos-fw firewall. Already tracked by the fork in docs/wireguard-rest-bind.md with a breakage analysis and a recommended fix (second restlisten on the wg address via extraConfig, leaving restAddress untouched).
impact: A single firewall failure (rule regression, misconfiguration) exposes the lnd admin API. Mitigations verified present: firewall-enabled and anti-nftables evaluation assertions, accept rule scoped to -i wg-nb and the single peer /32, restrictPeer REJECT inserted ahead of all accepts, and the wireguard-lndconnect VM test is in the release-gating CI matrix.
recommendation: Implement the documented second-listener design from docs/wireguard-rest-bind.md (extraConfig restlisten=${serverAddress}:${restPort} plus lnd-after-wireguard-wg-nb ordering), then re-run the adversarial audit per the fork's policy.

title: update-nix-bitcoin prints a malformed compare URL on first run
description: When nix-bitcoin-release.nix does not exist yet, $current is empty, so the extracted base commit is empty and the printed https://github.com/ostermayer/nix-bitcoin/compare/...<commit> URL is malformed. The operator is still directed to review the pinned commit before re-entering the shell.
impact: Cosmetic; no security impact. The no-auto-exec supply-chain fix itself is correct.
preconditions: First run of update-nix-bitcoin in a config dir without nix-bitcoin-release.nix.
recommendation: Print the commit URL (github.com/ostermayer/nix-bitcoin/commit/$commit) when no previous pin exists.

title: deriveaddresses in the public RPC whitelist is the largest remaining per-call CPU cost
description: The public (unprivileged-credential) whitelist deliberately excludes minutes-scale CPU calls (scantxoutset, getblocktemplate, gettxoutsetinfo) but keeps deriveaddresses. Bitcoin Core v31.1 caps descriptor ranges at 1,000,000 entries server-side (ParseDescriptorRange), bounding each call to roughly seconds-to-tens-of-seconds of CPU and a large JSON response.
impact: Bounded per call; only abusable by a holder of the public RPC credentials with network reachability to bitcoind's RPC port, which by default is localhost/netns-only. The whitelist header already instructs users who proxy this user publicly to narrow the list.
preconditions: User exposes the public RPC user beyond localhost (non-default).
recommendation: Optionally drop deriveaddresses (no local consumer in the fork's service set: lnd, electrs, nbxplorer, btcpayserver do not call it), or document it alongside the getpeerinfo/getnodeaddresses caveat.
